newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-MONACO TRY TO CONCENTRATE ON MATCH AGAINST LILLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO TRY TO CONCENTRATE ON MATCH AGAINST LILLE.

text.p: With a 10-point lead over nearest rivals Paris St Germain and the prospect of a showdown against Internazionale next week, Monaco are wary they could lose their concentration when they host Lille in a league match on Friday.

"It is true then when we walk on the pitch on Friday there is a risk our minds will be elsewhere," said in-form Brazilian striker Sonny Anderson. "But it is also true that we've managed to solve these sort of problems so far this season."
"We've prepared this match all the more seriously as we know it is the last step before meeting Internazionale."
Anderson said he badly wanted to score against Lille as a tribute to his newly born child Loic.
But PSG will face a 17th-placed Lille side who are battling against relegation and who will want to impress their new coaching team.
Former boss Jean-Michel Cavalli was replaced by Charly Samoy and Herve Gauthier, who have just seven matches left to save the team from northern France.
"We must all fight together with heart with guts," Gauthier said. "It won't be easy since we're meeting France's best two teams, Monaco and Paris St Germain, consecutively."
Goalkeeper Jean-Marie Aubry, who was with Angers when they were relegated three seasons ago, also warned his team mates.
"When you go down it is very difficult to make it back to the first division as a player," he said.
The team from the principality should be all the more cautious as they struggled to beat bottom-placed Nice in their last league outing.
Coach Jean Tigana admitted his players were a little tired.

Monaco had six internationals in action this week, four playing for France in a friendly against Sweden and striker Marco Grassi and midfielder John Collins called up by Switzerland and Scotland for World Cup qualifiers.
For Monaco, victory against Lille would serve two purposes.

It would maintain their comfortable league lead before two tricky away games in Bordeaux and Strasbourg, and it would boost their confidence ahead of their UEFA Cup semifinal first leg clash against Inter.
